title: SQLite-to-PostgreSQL backend boundary and table inventory

dispositionEnum.migrate: backend-owned state that becomes PostgreSQL rows under the single backend database
dispositionEnum.retain: Codex kernel, Device Client, or one-time local migration bookkeeping that stays on SQLite or embedded storage

contract.targetNaming: targetTable defaults to <pgSchema>.<sourceTable>; PG-020 may override per table but must keep entry ids stable
contract.migrationOrderInvariant: a row's migrationOrder must be >= the migrationOrder of every table its foreign keys reference; equal values migrate in one batch
contract.volumeCheck: checkSql runs against the SQLite database before cutover; expectation names the growth class PG-030 must re-verify

legacyTargets.verifiedClaim: exactly 7 tables: winwincode_schema_migrations, winwincode_product_state, winwincode_command_receipts, winwincode_outbox, winwincode_aggregate_journals, winwincode_aggregate_journal_records, winwincode_audit_outbox
legacyTargets.tenantRlsRemnants: every business table is FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with scope_key policies driven by current_setting('winwincode.scope_key')
legacyTargets.reason: v1 mirrors only the control-plane core event store; it omits auth, audit chain, event hub, observability, integration, artifact catalog, client/device, execution scheduling and identity tables, and it bakes in the retired multi-tenant RLS design. It is NOT the backend target; the canonical schema is redesigned under PG-020 on top of this inventory.
